Please read the manuscript in papers/investigations-5/01_heat_density_asymptotics/recurrence/, and the most recent summary notes/13_CHAT0003_RESULTS_SUMMARY_20261026.md. 

Let's discuss the results at a high level. Please describe what the new research has accomplished.
I’ll read the manuscript and latest summary, then explain the main advances and what remains unresolved. I’ll also follow the repository’s chat-history workflow.

The latest summary goes beyond the manuscript: it adds finite algorithms, explicit error constants, and certificate replays for two computational components. I’m checking how those additions build on the approximation theorems so I can distinguish the analytical results from the software work still ahead.

The central mathematical gain is a hierarchy whose accuracy improves in a controlled way as more terms are retained. The newer work makes that theory more concrete: it supplies terminating algorithms and an explicit height threshold, then tests certified gamma and quadrature components. The complete field evaluator is still unfinished, and the proved threshold is far too large to serve as a practical starting point.

The main accomplishment is **a systematically improvable approximation to the canonical Riemann heat flow, together with explicit algorithms and the first certified computational components.** The [manuscript](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/01_heat_density_asymptotics/recurrence/manuscript/main.tex) establishes the approximation theory; the [latest summary](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/01_heat_density_asymptotics/recurrence/notes/13_CHAT0003_RESULTS_SUMMARY_20261026.md) adds substantial progress toward evaluating it.

I see five main advances.

1. **There is now a systematic hierarchy of corrections.**  
   The research explains how to construct successive approximations and what accuracy each level buys. At fixed order \(p\), the proved error allowance in the natural gamma normalization is
   \[
   O\!\left(X^{-(p+3/4)}\right).
   \]
   Thus the first two levels give \(X^{-7/4}\) and \(X^{-11/4}\). These estimates control the field, its first three spatial derivatives, and its first time derivative together. A crucial discovery is that the arithmetic corrections and the Riemann–Siegel completion must advance together: order \(p\) requires completion through \(C_{2p}\) to support that rate.

2. **The hierarchy remains controlled when its order grows with height.**  
   This is the strongest analytical advance. The work tracks how the constants grow, allowing approximately \(\tfrac12\log X\) correction levels. On fixed complex neighborhoods and \(1\le T\le2\), it obtains
   \[
   \text{outer-envelope normalized error}\le
   \exp\!\left[-\frac14\log^2\!\left(\frac{X}{4\pi}\right)\right].
   \]
   That decays faster than every fixed inverse power of \(X\). The normalization uses a positive amplitude envelope, so the bound remains meaningful near zeros. The earlier ansatz work already had a separate growing-degree construction; this result establishes comparable accuracy for the new fluctuation hierarchy.

3. **The approximation stays tied to the complete canonical field.**  
   Both arithmetic arms, every retained mode, and the bounded correction integral remain present. Each frozen finite model satisfies the heat equation exactly, while separate estimates establish its closeness to the canonical solution. That combination matters: it provides compatible evolution and quantified approximation, including the derivatives needed for later applications.

4. **The newest research makes the analytical construction effective.**  
   Earlier evaluation statements depended on numerical ingredients meeting specified error contracts. The latest work supplies terminating constructions for those ingredients on the declared input class, improves the expensive gamma and quadrature procedures, and accounts for arithmetic cost and memory. It also replaces symbolic calibration constants with explicit values and proves a sufficient threshold covering every larger admissible height, including changes in truncation orders.

   The threshold is enormous, and the full calculation still processes roughly \(\sqrt X\) arithmetic modes. The achievement here is explicit computability with controlled errors; practical full-field performance remains unresolved.

5. **Some of that construction now exists as executable certificate-producing software.**  
   The latest work delivered and replayed 36 gamma cases and 15 base Gauss quadrature constructions—51 certificates in total—and rejected ten deliberately altered or invalid cases. This establishes bounded computational evidence for important components. The remaining Riemann–Siegel coefficient software, geometry, scaling, and complete field calculation still need implementation and certification.

My assessment is that this is **a substantive approximation and computation milestone**: the project can now explain how accuracy improves, how much precision is sufficient, and how numerical errors can be accounted for. The manuscript’s evaluation discussion lags these newest developments; the summary should govern that part of the current status.

The remaining mathematical bridge is from accurate field evaluation to the particular sign, zero-separation, or physical-observable estimates the broader program needs. Those conclusions have not yet been established. Following the [result-status conventions](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/result-summaries/README.md), [heat-flow record](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/result-summaries/11_newman_heat_flow_reductions_and_certificates.md), and [scope cautions](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/avoid/README.md), the analytical results are written proofs from named inputs, with internal assessments; [independent specialist validation remains open](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/avoid/05_same_model_reviews_and_shared_premises.md).

This sounds like very excellent progress. Please include all of the new results in the manuscript, feel free to rewrite it in any way you see fit to maximize clarity, narrative flow, and elegance of results without losing necessary detail. As always, please only reference numerics for backup support using links to the notes for details. Afterwards please make sure the research-overview and research-progress files are up to date with the most useful paths forward to strengthen the results, with analytic advancements primary and numerical checks used only in support of the analytic goals, and then please verify the chat history and write a continuation note.

I’ll integrate the new analytical results into the manuscript, keeping numerical evidence as brief supporting references. Then I’ll update the research overview and progress files around the strongest analytical next steps, check the manuscript, and save a continuation note with verified chat-history provenance.

I’m using the PDF skill to check the finished manuscript’s layout. I’ll organize the paper around three connected results: the approximation hierarchy, a finite evaluation construction, and explicit constants and cost bounds. The computational replay will remain a short supporting paragraph linked to its detailed note.

The new results support a stronger final theorem than the manuscript currently states: finite evaluation on a precisely defined input class, with explicit calibration and a sufficient height threshold. I’ll retain the earlier error-budget theorem as a reusable step in that proof. For future work, I’ll put sharper analytical bounds and a lower sufficient height first; component checks will support those goals.

The provider section now includes the exact input restrictions, pole-safe coefficient construction, and the distinction between delivered precision and internal arithmetic cost. I’m integrating the calibration proofs next so the final theorem states both its numerical constants and the domains where they hold. I’ve also rechecked the principal classical formulas used in those additions.

The integrated draft is now building. Its main text carries the stronger analytical results, while the detailed elementary algorithms sit in appendices to keep the argument readable. I’m updating the research agenda around a concrete next proof task: reduce the conservative height threshold while preserving the same error target, derivative bounds, and full arithmetic sum.

The revised manuscript now brings the finite algorithms, cost bounds, and explicit height threshold into the main argument. I’m checking the full PDF and finishing the research roadmap, with sharpening that threshold as the leading analytical next step.

The 42-page PDF has passed the layout check. The argument now progresses from approximation, through error budgets and finite constructions, to the explicit accuracy and cost theorems. The numerical results appear only as supporting references to the notes, as requested.

The manuscript and research-roadmap updates are installed. The roadmap now leads with proving a smaller sufficient height threshold, followed by stronger coefficient bounds and a joint time–height regime. I’m checking the installed build, then verifying the chat archive and writing the continuation note.

Both compilers pass with no LaTeX warnings or unresolved references, and the installed PDF matches the pages I inspected. All five recurrence chat archives also pass the integrity and identity checks. I’m saving the continuation note with the precise next proof task and its reading order.

The manuscript is now **42 pages**, integrating the finite algorithms, explicit calibration and height threshold, and evaluation cost bounds. I reorganized the argument for continuity, retained technical details in appendices, and kept numerics as supporting links to the notes.
